behaviours.title: Balance of an account never opened or used is 0
behaviours.given: a new Ledger with no accounts
behaviours.then: it returns 0 without error
behaviours.contrary_then: reading the balance of an unknown account throws an error
contrary_alternatives: it returns undefined
it returns NaN

behaviours.title: Entries of an unknown account is an empty list
behaviours.then: it returns an empty list []
behaviours.contrary_then: it returns undefined
contrary_alternatives: it throws an unknown-account error

behaviours.title: Opening an account starts it at balance 0 with no entries
behaviours.then: balance('A') is 0 and entries('A') is []
behaviours.contrary_then: the account starts with a non-zero opening balance of 100
contrary_alternatives: opening records an 'open' entry in the history

behaviours.title: Re-opening an existing account does not reset its balance or history
behaviours.given: account 'A' has received a deposit of 100 with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: balance('A') stays 100 and entries('A') still holds the single deposit of 100
behaviours.contrary_then: re-opening resets the balance to 0 and clears the history
contrary_alternatives: re-opening is rejected with an error because the account already exists

behaviours.title: Depositing into an unopened account opens it and credits it
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where 'A' was never opened
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 100 and entries('A') is [{ txnId: 't1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 100 }]
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected because the account does not exist and the balance stays 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted but no history entry is recorded

behaviours.title: Deposit of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 0 with no entries
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted as a no-op and the result is { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted and a zero-amount entry is recorded

behaviours.title: Deposit of -5 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 0 with no entries
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the negative amount is treated as a withdrawal of 5

behaviours.title: Deposit of NaN is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted and the balance becomes NaN
the deposit is accepted and treated as 0

behaviours.title: Smallest positive deposit of 0.01 is accepted
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') is 0.01
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected with 'invalid-amount' and the balance stays 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected because it is below a minimum deposit of 1

behaviours.title: Deposit amounts are rounded to cents; a half cent rounds up
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 0.13 and the entry amount is 0.13
behaviours.contrary_then: the half cent is rounded down (or to even) and the balance is 0.12
contrary_alternatives: the amount is stored unrounded as 0.125
the deposit is rejected because it has more than two decimals

behaviours.title: Deposit fractions below half a cent round down
behaviours.then: balance('A') is 10
behaviours.contrary_then: the fraction is always rounded up and the balance is 10.01
contrary_alternatives: the balance is kept unrounded at 10.004

behaviours.title: A positive deposit that rounds to 0 is accepted and recorded as 0
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 0 and an entry { txnId: 't1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 0 } is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected with 'invalid-amount' because it rounds to zero
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted and the balance becomes 0.004
the deposit is accepted but no entry is recorded

behaviours.title: Running balances are not re-rounded: 0.1 + 0.2 gives 0.30000000000000004
behaviours.contrary_then: balance('A') is exactly 0.3
contrary_alternatives: balances are tracked in integer cents and read back as 30

behaviours.title: Repeating a deposit txnId is reported ok but not applied again
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') stays 100 and there is still one entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the second deposit is applied and the balance becomes 200
contrary_alternatives: the second deposit is rejected with a 'duplicate' reason and the balance stays 100

behaviours.title: A txnId already used on one account is silently ignored on another account
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } but balance('B') is 0 and 'B' has no entries
behaviours.contrary_then: txnIds are per account, so 'B' is credited and its balance becomes 50
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected with a duplicate-transaction reason

behaviours.title: Amount validation happens before the duplicate check on deposit
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the duplicate txnId is detected first and the result is { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the call is rejected with a 'duplicate' reason

behaviours.title: A deposit txnId blocks a later withdrawal with the same txnId
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } but balance('A') stays 100 and only the deposit entry exists
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is applied and the balance becomes 60
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected with a duplicate-transaction reason

behaviours.title: Withdrawal debits the balance and records a withdrawal entry
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 70 and the new entry is { txnId: 'w1', kind: 'withdrawal', amount: 30 }
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected and the balance stays 100
contrary_alternatives: the entry records the amount as -30

behaviours.title: Withdrawing more than the balance is rejected as insufficient-funds
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes -50
contrary_alternatives: only 100 is paid out and the balance becomes 0

behaviours.title: Withdrawing exactly the whole balance is allowed
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected as insufficient-funds and the balance stays 100
contrary_alternatives: a minimum balance must remain, so it is rejected

behaviours.title: Withdrawing one cent more than the balance is rejected
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: a small overdraft tolerance allows it and the balance becomes -0.01

behaviours.title: The funds check uses the withdrawal amount after rounding to cents
behaviours.then: the amount rounds to 100, the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the unrounded 100.004 exceeds the balance so it is rejected as insufficient-funds
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected for having more than two decimals

behaviours.title: Withdrawing from an unknown account is refused as insufficient-funds
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('ghost') is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'unknown-account' }
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal goes through and the balance becomes -10

behaviours.title: Withdrawal of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted as a no-op with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted and a zero-amount entry is recorded

behaviours.title: Withdrawal of -10 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the negative withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes 110

behaviours.title: Withdrawal of NaN is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected as insufficient-funds

behaviours.title: Repeating a withdrawal txnId is reported ok but debited only once
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') stays 70
behaviours.contrary_then: the second withdrawal is applied and the balance becomes 40
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with a duplicate-transaction reason and the balance stays 70

behaviours.title: A rejected withdrawal does not use up its txnId
behaviours.given: account 'A' has 50 and withdraw('A', 80, 'w1') was rejected as insufficient-funds
behaviours.when: deposit('A', 50, 'd2') is made and withdraw('A', 80, 'w1') is retried
behaviours.then: the retry returns { ok: true } and balance('A') becomes 20
behaviours.contrary_then: the retry is treated as a duplicate: it returns ok but the balance stays 100
contrary_alternatives: the retry is rejected as a duplicate transaction

behaviours.title: Withdrawing exactly the daily limit of 5000 is allowed
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 10000 and no withdrawals yet
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') is 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with 'daily-limit' because the limit must not be reached
contrary_alternatives: the daily limit is lower (e.g. 1000) and the withdrawal is rejected

behaviours.title: A single withdrawal of 5000.01 breaches the daily limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 10000 and no withdrawals yet
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and balance('A') stays 10000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted with { ok: true } and the balance becomes 4999.99
contrary_alternatives: only 5000 is paid out and the rest refused

behaviours.title: The daily limit is cumulative across withdrawals
behaviours.given: account 'A' has 10000 and has already withdrawn 3000 (w1)
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and balance('A') stays 7000
behaviours.contrary_then: the limit applies per withdrawal, so it is accepted with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: only 2000 is paid out to reach the limit

behaviours.title: Cumulative withdrawals may reach exactly 5000
behaviours.given: account 'A' has 10000 and has already withdrawn 3000 (w1)
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') is 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with 'daily-limit' and the balance stays 7000
contrary_alternatives: only one withdrawal per day is allowed so the second is refused

behaviours.title: The daily limit is tracked per account
behaviours.given: accounts 'A' and 'B' each have 10000 and 'A' has already withdrawn 5000
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('B') is 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the limit is shared across the ledger and 'B' is rejected with 'daily-limit'
contrary_alternatives: the limit is per customer and applies to both accounts together

behaviours.title: A rejected withdrawal does not consume the daily limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' has 10000 and withdraw('A', 5000.01, 'w1') was rejected with 'daily-limit'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') is 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the rejected attempt counted toward the limit and this one is rejected with 'daily-limit'
contrary_alternatives: the account is blocked from withdrawing for the day after a limit breach

behaviours.title: Insufficient funds is reported ahead of the daily limit
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' }
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted as an overdraft

behaviours.title: Transfers are not subject to or counted in the daily withdrawal limit
behaviours.when: transfer('A', 'B', 6000, 't1') is made and then withdraw('A', 5000, 'w1')
behaviours.then: both return { ok: true }; balance('A') is 9000 and balance('B') is 6000
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected with 'daily-limit' because it exceeds 5000
contrary_alternatives: the transfer succeeds but consumes the limit, so the withdrawal is rejected with 'daily-limit'

behaviours.title: Transfer moves money, opens the recipient and records transfer-out and transfer-in entries
behaviours.given: account 'A' has 100 and 'B' was never opened
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }; balance('A') is 70, balance('B') is 30; 'A' gets { txnId: 't1', kind: 'transfer-out', amount: 30 } and 'B' gets { txnId: 't1', kind: 'transfer-in', amount: 30 }
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected because 'B' does not exist and 'B' stays at 0
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is accepted but only recorded in the sender's history

behaviours.title: Transferring the whole balance is allowed
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 0 and balance('B') is 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected as insufficient-funds and balances stay 100 and 0
contrary_alternatives: a minimum balance must remain so it is rejected

behaviours.title: Transferring one cent more than the balance is rejected
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }; balances stay 100 and 0 and no entries are added
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is accepted with { ok: true } and 'A' goes to -0.01
contrary_alternatives: only the available 100 is moved

behaviours.title: Transfer of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is accepted as a no-op with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is accepted and zero-amount entries are recorded

behaviours.title: Transfer of -10 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is accepted with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is accepted, moving 10 from 'B' to 'A'

behaviours.title: Repeating a transfer txnId is reported ok but moves money only once
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }; balance('A') stays 70 and balance('B') stays 30
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is applied again, leaving 'A' at 40 and 'B' at 60
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with a duplicate-transaction reason

behaviours.title: Transfer amounts are rounded to cents; a half cent rounds up
behaviours.then: balance('B') is 0.13 and the transfer-in entry amount is 0.13
behaviours.contrary_then: the half cent is rounded down and balance('B') is 0.12
contrary_alternatives: balance('B') is the unrounded 0.125

behaviours.title: Transfer to the same account leaves the balance unchanged but records two entries
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') stays 100 and 'A' gets both a transfer-out and a transfer-in entry after its deposit
behaviours.contrary_then: a transfer to the same account is rejected
contrary_alternatives: the self-transfer is accepted but records nothing

behaviours.title: entries returns a copy; changing it does not change the ledger history
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a single deposit of 100
behaviours.when: the caller empties the list returned by entries('A')
behaviours.then: a fresh entries('A') still has 1 entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the ledger history is emptied and entries('A') returns 0 entries
contrary_alternatives: entries returns a frozen list and the caller's change throws
